title: fix(core)!: the offboarding hand-over leaves the owner of a controlled_by_parent detail where it is
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg6v19uPsX6gX42G8tGcvvzb)_
Fixes #35344

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — the hand-over stops counting and moving `owner_id` on `controlled_by_parent` details
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no published skill teaches the assigned-work hand-over (`git grep assigned-work -- skills` answers 0 hits on this head); the admin guide is updated here

## 维护者速读

- 用户看到的变化：封禁员工做工作交接时，工时、报销明细、行项目这类跟随主记录的明细不再把负责人转给接手人，也不再算进待交接数量；其它对象的负责人和明细上的审批人等照旧交接。
- 为什么：明细的负责人记的是谁干的活，转过去后接手人看上去像录了离职者的工时、花了离职者的钱，审批和报表读错。
- 如果判断错：少数没挂主记录的明细行，离职者被封禁后只有能查看全部的人看得到；撤回本次合并即恢复，无数据迁移。
- 需要您做的：无。

## What changes

- `userAssignedWorkFields` (`@objectstack/core`) leaves the owner column (`owner_id`) of an object whose `sharingModel` is `controlled_by_parent` out of the roster. Both the count (`GET .../assigned-work`) and the transfer (`POST .../assigned-work/transfer`) read that roster, so the detail's owner is neither counted nor moved — including a transfer whose `objects` names the detail alone.
- Unchanged: the detail's own user fields (an `approver`, an `assignee`), and `owner_id` on every object whose `sharingModel` is `private`, `public_read`, `public_read_write` or unset.
- Admin guide (`content/docs/permissions/administrator-guide.mdx`) says so; patch changeset on `@objectstack/core` with the BREAKING banner and an ADR-0087 disposition.

**Shape shipped: left out, not counted-not-moved.** The preferred shape counts the detail's owner rows as `transferable: false`. The REST answer already carries that field, so no new public field was needed, but the ban dialog words every `transferable: false` row as "Lists several people, so it cannot be handed over here." That sentence is false for a single-valued owner column. A truthful sentence needs a new translated string in the seven UI locale catalogues, which are outside this claim's file surface. So the rows are left out and the panel is untouched. Counting them belongs with the object-level switch follow-up, where the panel learns a reason.

**The predicate.** `@objectstack/spec` exports no object-level "is this a detail" predicate. The named one, `masterGovernsRowWrites` (`@objectstack/plugin-security`), lives in a package that depends on `@objectstack/core`, so core cannot import it. The reading is therefore spelled once in this module (`accessFollowsMaster`). It reads the flat and nested spots the same way the access gates do, so the hand-over treats as a detail exactly the objects whose rows the gates answer through a master. The owner column is matched by `SystemFieldName.OWNER_ID`.

## Tests

<details><summary>core: the module's file, the whole package, typecheck (head 3ae0a436fd)</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/security/user-assigned-work.test.ts` → `Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 19 passed (19)` (13 before + 6 new).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core test` → `Test Files 153 passed (153) · Tests 3632 passed (3632)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core typecheck` → exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/user-work-routes.test.ts` (serves this module, reads core's rebuilt `dist`) → `Tests 7 passed (7)`.

New pins (`a controlled_by_parent detail keeps its owner in the hand-over`):
1. The roster leaves the detail's `owner_id` out and keeps the detail's `approver` and the master's `owner_id`.
2. The nested `security.sharingModel` spot is read as well.
3. Twin: the same object under `private` / `public_read` / `public_read_write` / unset keeps `owner_id`.
4. The count does not report the detail's owner.
5. The transfer moves the master's owner and the detail's approver, never the detail's owner.
6. A transfer naming only the detail moves its approver, leaves its owner, and never queries the owner column.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (one-shot, fix committed first)</summary>

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs --file packages/core/src/security/user-assigned-work.ts --anchor "if (detail && field === SystemFieldName.OWNER_ID) continue;" --delete -- vitest run src/security/user-assigned-work.test.ts`: anchor 1 → 0, blob `789aa438f8a9` → `c90797db9690`. Five of the new pins went red. The twin (pin 3) stayed green, as it should. Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- …`: the blob is back to `789aa438f8a9…`, equal to the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The test imports the module by relative path, so there is no `dist` leg.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The detail predicate reads `sharingModel` (flat or nested) the same way the platform's other access readers do (plugin-security, plugin-sharing, objectql each spell it). Lifting one object-level predicate into `@objectstack/spec/data` would let all of them share it. That is an observation, not a filing.
- Corner: an optional-master detail (`master_detail` declared `required: false`) row that names no master is read by its owner and by View All. After this change a banned owner's such rows keep that owner, so only View All reads them. This follows the maintainer's derived default (transfer off on a detail). An author who wants those owners moved needs the object-level switch.
- The UI panel is untouched: it already offers the hand-over only for rows the server answers `transferable: true`, and the detail's owner rows are no longer in the answer.

## Verification

<details><summary>Local gates (head 3ae0a436fd)</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 97 families, all run locally. The `--ran` reconciliation: `✓ 97 derived famil(ies) accounted for`. 95 exited 0. Two exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, nothing measured), both because packages this diff does not touch have no `dist` (`client-react`, the adapters and apps). They are NOT MEASURED locally and left to CI:
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples`
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`

`overlap-check` answers `VERDICT clean` against `origin/main`. Every repo-wide family, `test:repo` and the full farm are CI's. The full dogfood battery owed by the `(narrowing)` arm is reported in the dev report.
</details>

## Fix round (contract review 7006025069)

Prose only, head `26ff98c888`; no behaviour change and no new conjunct.

- **S1, the optional-master row class.** The module docblock, the administrator guide and the changeset no longer say a detail's access always follows its master. They now name the row class: a detail row whose master reference is empty, on an optional master (`required: false`, ADR-0055 as amended). For that row they say:
  - who reaches it: its owner reads and writes it, beside View All / Modify All on the detail;
  - what this change does to it: its owner is not counted or moved, so after the ban only View All / Modify All holders reach it;
  - the remedy that exists: a holder of Modify All on the detail filters the detail by owner and edits the owner by hand.

  The docblock sentence now reads "On a detail the owner records who did the work, not who holds it". It adds that a row naming its master is reached through that master.
- **N1.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in this body and in the changeset (the diff widens nothing). The `!`, the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker are unchanged.
- N2, N3 and N4 go to the follow-up card.

<details><summary>Checks on 26ff98c888</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core typecheck` exit 0.
- `user-assigned-work.test.ts`: Tests 19 passed (19).
- The derived changeset and docs families: 34 families (the ADR-0087 registration, changeset-no-major, empty-changeset, changeset-gate self-tests, `check:docs`, doc-authoring and the rest of the docs set, nul-bytes, issue citations), all exit 0. The derived list is identical to the one on 3ae0a436fd.
- `overlap-check`: VERDICT clean. Not merged with `main` (no conflict).
- The full dogfood battery on the new head is recorded in the dev report on the card.
</details>
